passage:
A glass jar sat on the teacher's desk. Every time someone did something kind, another student could write it on a small piece of paper and put it in the jar.
At first, the jar filled slowly. Students only wrote big things, like helping someone who fell down. Then the teacher explained that small kindness also counted.
Soon, the jar filled with notes: "Amy lent me an eraser," "Ken waited for me," "Lisa shared her umbrella," and "Our class cleaned the floor without being asked."
At the end of the month, the teacher read the notes aloud. Many students were surprised that their small actions had been noticed.
The jar did not create kindness. It made kindness visible.
